evidence.note: go test ./internal/fsm/converge/ -covermode=count reports 100.0% of statements; 36 source mutations applied to converge.go in an out-of-tree copy of the repo (scratchpad) were killed except the six recorded below, so the suite is genuinely load-bearing for AllFixed, max_iterations off-by-one, budget/no_fixation_progress comparison direction, Payload redaction and deep-copy, DisallowUnknownFields, exit-code handling, not-Class=custom, MaxDepth/MaxAtoms bounds, top-level all_fixed restriction, compound error abort, compound Class/Name/Reason joins, and Describe's Validate delegation.

snap()'s claim that tokens are spread over the non-Input counters is true: Output=t/2, CacheRead=t-t/2-t/4, Reasoning=t/4 sums exactly to t for every value used (7, 10, 99, 100), so a Total() reading only Input would fail; verified against run/types.go:133.

The redaction assertions are real, not tautological: mutating Payload to skip sha256 hashing, to keep NodeOutputs, or to use a shallow copy instead of Clone all fail the test. run.Snapshot.Clone (types.go:237) does deep-copy Vars, so the no-mutation assertion at line 143 is meaningful.

EventTypes lists exactly the 16 declared Type* constants with no omission or duplicate; consumed by run/fold.go:331 knownType and machine.go:1028 sortedEventTypes. The header claim that the machine sets everything except Seq and Prev matches machine.go:441 stamp() (no Seq/Prev) and run/store.go:146-147 (Append sets them); Origin is set on the fork path at machine/fork.go:229. Pure type declarations, no logic; go vet clean.

OverflowHandlerData is field-for-field identical to CmdCallData but is NOT redundant: run/fold.go:173 and :177 discriminate on the concrete type, and the double audit (cmd_call by the runner + overflow_handler by the machine) is specified in docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-core.md:437. Its Stdout/Stderr are covered by export redaction (export.go:407, export_test.go:174).

Fingerprint stabilization is verified: reverting to the reason-suffixed form in a scratch copy fails internal/reviewers/sharded_test.go:207-209. The legacy prefix 'epic:context-risk:' at internal/findings/findings.go:201 ends in a colon and so cannot alias the new colon-free id.

The De Morgan rewrite of the no-eval intent guard is provably equivalent to the prior !(A||B||C) form; go test ./internal/reviewers/ passes and mutating the whole condition to true or false is killed, so both branches are exercised.

findings.note: Comment claims a property the test does not check. The comment says 'A multi-document node is rejected too', but the node constructed is &yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.DocumentNode} with zero Content - an EMPTY document, which is what the t.Fatal message on the next line actually says. Verified by mutation: relaxing converge.go:113 from `len(node.Content) != 1` to `len(node.Content) < 1` (which accepts a multi-document node and silently parses only its first document) leaves the whole package green. The multi-document rejection is unverified. yaml.Unmarshal only ever decodes the first document, so the case is reachable only from hand-built nodes, which is exactly what this test constructs - it just does not build one. Fix: add `multi.Content = []*yaml.Node{scalar, scalar}` or drop the word 'multi-document' from the comment.

findings.note: The stated rationale for MaxDepth and MaxAtoms is false, and the test that pins both boundaries never checks the invariant they exist for. converge.go:66 says 'MaxDepth bounds nesting so composite names stay within run.MaxShort' and converge.go:69 says MaxAtoms bounds leaves 'for the same reason'. Measured empirically in an out-of-tree copy: `any:` with MaxAtoms(32) children, each `{not: {not: {not: {cmd: <32-char name>}}}}` (the deepest legal shape, since a top-level any's children start at depth 1 and depth 4 is accepted), is accepted by Validate and yields a Predicate.Name() of 1668 bytes against run.MaxShort = 1024 (run/types.go:41). Cmd names are capped at 32 chars by workflow.go:267, so this is the true worst case and it exceeds the bound by 63%. No functional break: machine.go:775 does run.CapText(r.Atom, run.MaxShort) before the converge event and CapText accounts for canonical-encoding overhead, so fold.go:574's shortOK never rejects the row - but the truncation is silently discarded (`atom, _ :=`) and the comment tells a maintainer that no truncation can occur. TestC4ValidateAndParseErrors pins acceptance at exactly MaxAtoms and MaxDepth without ever asserting the resulting Name() length.

evidence.note: // MaxDepth bounds nesting so composite names stay within run.MaxShort. - measured worst case is 1668 vs MaxShort 1024
// MaxAtoms bounds the number of leaves for the same reason.
'at MaxAtoms' asserts acceptance only; no assertion on the composite name length
'at MaxDepth' likewise
atom, _ := run.CapText(r.Atom, run.MaxShort) - the truncation flag that would surface the overrun is discarded

findings.note: The 'all partial' case covers only the first-child-quiet path, so half of compound's `all` short-circuit is untested despite 100% statement coverage (the block is entered, just always by kid[0]). snap(4, 4, intp(5), 0, 5) makes no_fixation_progress quiet, so Evaluate returns at the first iteration and the accumulator branch is never reached with a non-empty names slice. Verified by mutation: adding `if !r.Stop && len(names) > 0 { return Result{Stop: true, Atom: "BOGUS", ...} }` to converge.go:323 - i.e. an `all` that reports a stop when a LATER child is quiet - leaves the package green. Fix: add a case where the first child fires and a later one does not, e.g. all: [no_fixation_progress, {max_iterations: 5}] against snap(0, 5, intp(5), 0, 5).

findings.note: The 'cmd-empty' bad case passes for the wrong reason, so the empty-name guard it names is untested. TestC4 runs every bad case through Validate(node, []string{"notify"}); with cmdNames non-nil, `{cmd: ''}` is rejected by the unknown-cmd branch at converge.go:168 before the name=="" guard at converge.go:165 can matter. Verified by mutation: deleting `|| name == ""` from converge.go:165 leaves the package green. The guard is only reachable through Parse (cmdNames nil, the MustParse path the machine uses at machine.go:426), and no test exercises Parse with an empty cmd name - so a workflow that somehow reached Parse with `{cmd: ''}` would bind a cmdAtom named 'cmd:' and shell out to the empty name. Fix: assert `Parse(node(t, "{cmd: ''}"), nil)` returns ERR_BAD_CONVERGENCE alongside the existing non-string-cmd case at line 297.

evidence.note: {"cmd-empty", "{cmd: ''}"} in the bad table, validated with cmdNames=["notify"]
if err := val.Decode(&name); err != nil || name == "" - the name=="" half is dead under the test's cmdNames
cmdNames != nil && !contains(cmdNames, name) is what actually rejects the empty name in the test

findings.note: Budget key-name validation is untested. findings.note: One third of the error-abort assertion cannot fail. The loop at line 219 runs three sources through the same `len(fr.calls) != 1` check, but the third, "not: {cmd: c}", contains exactly one cmd atom, so fr.calls can never have more than one entry regardless of whether the error actually aborts evaluation. For that entry the assertion is a tautology; the two compound sources carry the real signal (mutating compound.Evaluate to `continue` on error is killed). Cosmetic, but it inflates the apparent strength of the check.

if len(fr.calls) != 1 - unfalsifiable for the not: source
